articles.title_orig: 65 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Screaming Deals' Sale (North America)
articles.title_zh: 65 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Screaming Deals' Sale (North America)
articles.content_orig:
Nintendo is welcoming the spooky season the only way it knows how: with a big old eShop sale, of course!
The ' Screaming Deals ' sale is now live on the North American eShop, bringing welcome discounts to a whole host of Switch 1 and 2 bangers until 31st October at 11:59 PT — so make sure you've made the most of it by then!
There are so many games on sale, in fact, that we have assembled the following list to showcase the cream of the crop, pulling every 'Screaming Deals' game we rated a 9/10 or higher (plus one personal pick from those that fell below the review bar, because we couldn't resist).
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 854k
As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store .
Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.
We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.
Alien: Isolation is a survival horror masterpiece and straight-up one of the very best horror video games ever released.
It's a nerve-wracking affair — a slow, methodical game of cat and mouse against a brilliantly clever recreation of one of cinema's most infamous killers — but if you're up to the task you'll find one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences in the genre; a brilliant and beautiful homage to one of the greatest sci-fi movies of all time.
Feral Interactive has done a stellar job with this Switch port and the excellent motion controls and inclusion of all previously-released DLC only go to sweeten the deal. This is essential stuff for survival horror fans.
Developer Shared Memory's stated goal was “to craft complete experiences that will be playable long after the world loses its internet connection,” and screen after screen, Animal Well excels in delighting your eyes and giving your brain something to stew on.
It’s a riposte against a culture of post-launch updates in favour of a meticulously crafted, singular vision with potentially years’ worth of discoveries baked in. By all indications, Animal Well delivers on that long-term promise and does so with a one-of-a-kind elegance.
A slice of Viking strategic combat right out of the heart of Scandinavia’s indie development scene, Bad North was at the vanguard of a wave of smart yet intrinsically accessible real-time strategy titles.
Swedish developer Plausible Concept calls it ‘micro-strategy’ and it's the perfect encapsulation of a minimalist approach that covers everything from unit management to the Monument Valley -style isometric art style.
With enough enemy variance to convince you you’re playing an interactive episode of the Vikings TV show, this endlessly entertaining sea of bitesize battles will teach you to fear — and love — the sound of the oncoming horde.
Balatro is a roguelike for gamers who don't like roguelikes... and then everybody else on top of that. It utterly nails what it sets out to do, providing an instantly accessible, satisfying, and addictive gameplay loop that anybody can grasp.
It's an immensely enjoyable experience from the start, but as you get deeper in, there's really nothing else quite like it. Sublime.
It looks like The Witness and it plays a bit like StreetPass Garden , but Botany Manor blooms into something that's not only entirely its own, but also something quite special. Don't let its cosy aesthetics fool you — Botany Manor is packed with nicely challenging, well-designed puzzles, and isn't afraid to tackle heavy subjects, too.
As an adventure game, Chicory: A Colorful Tale is quite sincerely up there with the very best of the genre.
There’s plenty to see and do and a full completion run will probably take you 25-30 hours. The characters and their travails are rich and likeable, the game’s sense of humour is generally inspired, and it’s all very sweet without being sugary-twee and talking down to the player. It’s also an affecting little tearjerker that will definitely strike a chord if you make art, and almost certainly will even if you don’t – so long as you’re capable of pretty basic empathy.
Chicory is simple to play but impressively long and complex, with perfect controls, performance and visuals. Throw yourself into painting the world and you’ll be left with a game that’s very much your own and speaks to you directly – a beautiful marriage of mechanics, themes and visuals.
While it’s a shame that there are fewer games here than in other Konami collections — we’d have loved to have seen NES title Contra Force or the now-extinct WiiWare title Contra ReBirth — the ones included in the Contra Anniversary Collection are universally brilliant. The 8-bit and 16-bit Contra games are among the finest examples of the run ‘n gun genre, and to have almost all of them included in a single release and emulated flawlessly is an absolute treat.
Whether you’re a fan of the series or a curious onlooker who’s always wanted to see what the fuss was all about, this is essential.
We really like Crawl , and we’d bet our collected stash of gold and wrath you will, too. A dungeon-crawling hack-and-slash affair with roguelike elements, one player is the hero trying to get through a dungeon and the others play as monster-controlling ghosts attempting to kill said hero and take their place.
It's an everyone-for-themselves free-for-all, yet there are opportunities for frantic 3v1 co-operative play — a necessity when all the non-hero ghost characters must take joint control of bosses the hero faces. It’s great fun in single-player thanks to some aggressive AI, but that consistent danger takes on a new dimension when you and three of your friends are jostling for XP and that all-important killing blow.
Competitive couchplay doesn’t get much better than this on Switch.
In 2023, a year dominated by titanic, big-budget releases like Tears of the Kingdom and Mario Wonder , off-the-wall roguelike Dave The Diver stepped up to the plate and knocked the ball clear of the park with a heaving swing.
Its charming animations and writing supplement a mechanically dense experience that never stops dangling a new carrot to chase. You owe it to yourself to pick up this outstandingly funny, enthralling, and weird gem.
Death's Door is a modern classic, utilising old gameplay ideas in a new setting to make for a short and sweet experience you won’t want to miss. The snappy combat, rewarding exploration, and relaxing music will stick with you once you've finished, and while it may not have anything 'new' to offer, Death’s Door is so high quality that you’ll hardly have time to think about its lack of innovation.
Any fans of Zelda or Soulslike games will adore this - Acid Nerve has crafted an experience that’s absolutely worth your time and money.
An attractive art style, strong combat system, and meaningful player choices make Dicefolk a brilliant addition to the library, as it manages to feel fresh without getting too far away from the core ideas that make these sorts of games so addictive and popular.
Dicefolk is a good entry point to the genre, in fact; approachable without being patronising and it’s tons of fun once you get a grasp of it

articles.title_orig: A permanent Pokémon retail store is coming to London, the first of several planned to open outside Asia
articles.title_zh: A permanent Pokémon retail store is coming to London, the first of several planned to open outside Asia
articles.content_orig:
The Pokémon Company has announced that a permanent Pokémon retail store is coming to London.
The store, which is due to open “by 2029,” is “the first of several permanent Pokémon stores that are planned to launch outside of Asia,” according to The Pokémon Company .
A Pokémon retail location did exist outside of Asia between 2001 and 2005, when Pokémon Center New York was open. The store then became the Nintendo Store, which it remains to this day.
Notably, The Pokémon Company isn’t calling the store a Pokémon Center, the branding used for permanent Pokémon retail stores in Japan and pop-up stores at Pokémon events.
The exact location of the store has yet to be announced.
Pokémon retail locations typically feature exclusive merchandise, in addition to merchandise that’s available on the Pokémon Center website. As the UK is one of the few regions with a dedicated Pokémon Center retail website and fufillment center, it makes sense as the first location to recieve the permanent retail store.
Chief product and experience officer at The Pokémon Company International, Gaku Susai, commented: “We are always exploring new opportunities that help us create unique and memorable experiences for our fans. This new London store will give visitors the chance to step into the world of Pokémon, whether they’re discovering the brand for the first time or have been Trainers for years.
“We hope it becomes a place where everyone can come together, feel like part of a community and enjoy the magic of Pokémon in a whole new way.”
London has become a hub of Pokémon events in recent years. The Pokémon European International Championships have taken place at London’s Excel Center for several years. These events also feature a pop-up Pokémon Center, free slots for which regularly sell out weeks ahead of time.

articles.title_orig: How We Draw Lines in a World Awash in A.I. Images
articles.title_zh: How We Draw Lines in a World Awash in A.I. Images
articles.content_orig:
When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn't affect our editorial independence .
I remember when AI images were easy to spot thanks to dead giveaways like freakishly mutated hands, warped faces, and Escher-like architecture. That was way back in 2023. Since then, things have progressed fast. AI image generators now are so good that it’s genuinely hard to tell what’s real and what isn’t.
But that doesn’t stop us humans from thinking we still have an eye for what’s real and what’s fake. So if you still think you’ve got it, then go ahead and give it a try with Slop Sense . It’s a free website with a handful of games that put your AI-detecting skills to the test.
My favorite game is called Reality Check where you’re shown an image and have to guess whether it’s a real photo or an AI-generated one. You get 10 seconds to make each guess and 60 seconds to rack up as many points as possible.
You’ll earn points for correct guesses, lose points for mistakes, and get bonuses for stringing together correct answers. When the timer runs out, you can go back through the images and see which ones tripped you up. It even provides the prompt used to generate the AI images. My score was shockingly abysmal at 12 out of 22 correct.
There’s also Ghostwriter, which takes the same idea but asks you to guess which text is written by AI and which is written by humans. I actually found this to be easier, but that may be because my job involves actually writing text all day.
These are a fun time waster and if nothing else, they’re an eye opening experience for how convincing AI-generated images and text are becoming—think about that the next time you’re mindlessly scrolling through social media confidently thinking you know what’s AI slop and what’s not.
Oh, and the irony of using AI to build games about spotting AI isn’t lost on me.
For more fun and helpful tips, tricks, website and app recommendations, be sure to subscribe to our PCWorld Try This newsletter .

articles.title_orig: Shark Returns to Sea After Over a Month Stuck in a South Korean Port Canal
articles.title_zh: Shark Returns to Sea After Over a Month Stuck in a South Korean Port Canal
articles.content_orig:
SEOUL, South Korea — After failed attempts in recent weeks, South Korean officials on Wednesday finally freed a large gray shark that had been trapped for more than a month in a canal in the port city of Busan.
Officials used a floating platform to herd the nearly 10-foot female dusky shark, nicknamed Bukangi after the Korean name for Busan’s North Port, along the narrow canal for hours. The shark lingered at the canal’s mouth but eventually swam to sea, Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo said.
The shark was first spotted in mid-September and became a major tourist attraction as it slowly circled the canal, its fins slicing through the water’s surface.
Shark freed after a month trapped in South Korea canal
Busan officials, who made Bukangi a city mascot, said the shark attracted more than 1.7 million visitors to the canal. But they struggled for weeks to find a way to guide it back to the open sea.
Wednesday’s operation was the third attempt to free Bukangi, following failed efforts on Sept. 29 and Oct. 2 that involved boats spraying streams of water and nets placed across the narrow waterway. The shark avoided the boats and swam over the nets.
Experts have raised concerns about the shark’s condition, saying it had shown no signs of feeding during its monthlong stay in the canal and that falling water temperatures posed additional health risks.
Wednesday’s operation involved painstakingly maneuvering a large floating platform through the canal to drive the shark out. Workers stood on the platform and used oars to push Bukangi back whenever it approached. Dozens of other workers on both banks pulled ropes to drag the structure forward, as hundreds of onlookers lined the canal to watch the highly unusual rescue effort.
Workers managed to push the platform about a kilometer (0.6 miles) toward the mouth of the canal and placed additional netting in front of the structure to prevent the shark from swimming back in.
It wasn’t immediately clear how far the shark swam out and South Korea’s Yonhap news agency reported that it was seen at a nearby pier.
“We will never forget the great interest people have shown for Bukangi and Busan’s waters,” Chun wrote on Facebook. “We hope Bukangi can live a healthy life in the blue sea.”

articles.title_orig: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
articles.title_zh: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
articles.content_orig:
The new two-stage browser warning makes it easier to distinguish between shifty and dangerous URLs.﻿
The new two-stage browser warning makes it easier to distinguish between shifty and dangerous URLs.﻿
Google is launching a new browser safety feature for Chrome that aims to keep you better informed about how malicious a website might be before you open it. The new suspicious site warnings, available when Chrome’s Enhanced Protection is on, build on a similar two-stage system introduced for Chrome file downloads in 2024 , which provides visually different notifications for blocked files based on whether they’re determined to be “suspicious” or “dangerous.”
For the Chrome site warnings, the feature will flag a website as suspicious if it detects that it has similar qualities to other sites associated with phishing, malware, and scams. Google describes this warning as having a “lower confidence verdict” with possible risk of user harm — meaning there’s a chance it could be incorrectly flagged, but you should only proceed to the site if you’re 100 percent confident that it’s safe to do so. The warnings on “dangerous” website have a higher confidence verdict and “high risk of user harm,” however, and should be avoided entirely.
It’s easy to distinguish between these warnings at a glance. The notifications for suspicious websites will appear as a pop-up window on both desktop and mobile, with the webpage visible but darkened underneath, and an option to “Mark as safe” if the site was flagged mistakenly. The already familiar notification for dangerous sites is much harder to ignore: the warning message takes up almost the entire screen and the website will be replaced with a solid red background.
Google also improved Gemini-powered scam detection for Enhanced Protection users, alongside introducing the browser warning redesign.
Update, October 20th : Clarified that the suspicious site warnings appear when Enhanced Protection mode is on.

Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes.
Microsoft’s Advanced Shader Delivery works by offloading shader compilation for different hardware combinations to the cloud. “Using DirectX 12, Windows 11, and the Microsoft Agility SDK, developers capture shaders into a State Object Database (SODB), allowing Microsoft’s cloud network to precompile shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations,” explains Nvidia’s Andrew Burnes .
Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 now both support Advanced Shader Delivery, as long as you download the games via the Xbox PC app. “This system is storefront-agnostic, meaning you benefit even when playing games purchased on Steam, as long as the Xbox PC app is installed on your PC,” says Burnes.
Advanced Shader Delivery will let you skip the annoying shader compilation screen in Call of Duty , and it should improve the overall performance of supported games. “With a near-100 percent cache hit rate, it eliminates mid-game ‘just-in-time’ shader compilation, wiping out CPU spikes and frame stutters in titles like Gears of War: E-Day , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .
You can download Nvidia’s latest 621.01 update here , and Advanced Shader Delivery is also supported on AMD GPUs with Adrenalin 26.6.1 or higher and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 series with driver version 2026.08.3 or higher .

articles.title_orig: Xbox Game Pass Heading For A Massive Shakeup, Report Says
articles.title_zh: Xbox Game Pass Heading For A Massive Shakeup, Report Says
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft is reportedly planning a substantial revamp of Xbox Game Pass that will allow subscribers to choose the features they want in an à la carte fashion. The report comes by way of a new Fortune profile piece on Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
"Xbox is planning a major overhaul of Game Pass that would have players choose features à la carte," Fortune wrote, "including add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer, with the system operating on a tiered structure, according to people familiar with the strategy."
The piece dug in on Xbox's controversial subscription gaming purchase, noting the challenges faced about the service internally: "Game Pass, a Netflix-style monthly gaming service, helped Xbox build a subscription business. But it also led to a cannibalization of sales for the company’s higher-priced first-party game titles, especially during the critical launch period. And competing internal metrics within different teams — such as subscription revenue versus store revenue — exacerbated the problem, said former employees."
Fortune's piece also addresses a next-gen Xbox handheld as well as the next-gen Project Helix console, suggesting that, as rumored, it won't be cheap — unless Microsoft chooses to subsidize any of the cost.
A Game Pass revamp would be only the latest in a series of bold moves by Sharma, who has been on the job barely six months and has already cut the price of Game Pass Ultimate, signed Hideo Kojima's next-gen Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor project Physint , started two new verticals within Xbox, and handed development of Halo to Activision , to name a few. She's even found time to personally respond to customer support tickets and check out the latest build of The Elder Scrolls 6.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title_orig: After A Year Of Layoffs, Disney Finds $180 Million For Recruits From Bankrupt Character.AI
articles.title_zh: After A Year Of Layoffs, Disney Finds $180 Million For Recruits From Bankrupt Character.AI
articles.content_orig:
Sign up to get our news digest — delivered directly to your inbox twice a week.
Disney has spent much of 2026 cutting jobs and announcing restrictions on employee benefits, with the reductions continuing under new CEO Josh D’Amaro. Now, it plans to spend roughly $180 million over three years to compensate and retain 66 recruits from the recently bankrupt, highly controversial chatbot startup Character.AI.
According to Business Insider , citing bankruptcy filings, the hiring follows September layoffs that included technology workers. The recruits are following former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand, whom Disney recently appointed its first company-wide chief technology officer. The group crossing over constitutes most of Character.AI’s approximately 86-person workforce at September’s end.
As we reported last week , Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 protection on October 12, ten days after Anand officially joined Disney. Disney separately offered $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to certain intellectual property and certain company claims, subject to the bankruptcy sale process.
The spending adds another revealing chapter to Disney’s year of restructuring and continued efforts to get ahead in the AI race. The company eliminated jobs in January, approximately 1,000 more in April, and hundreds in July, including roughly 150 at Pixar .
In September, Disney’s top lawyer warned employees that his department would shrink substantially as the company considered automation, outside providers, and outsourcing. Beginning in 2027, Disney will also restrict spousal health coverage when spouses can obtain insurance through their own employers, even if those plans offer worse benefits.
These decisions come alongside substantial profits and shareholder payouts. Disney reported $5.6 billion in fiscal third-quarter segment operating income, up 21%, and raised its fiscal-year share-buyback target to at least $9 billion.
Big picture, the layoffs, benefit restrictions, buybacks, and AI hiring reveal consistent spending priorities. Disney is willing to commit substantial sums to AI expertise (remember its proposed $1 billion investment in OpenAI, announced alongside a Sora licensing deal that collapsed just over three months later, before any money changed hands?) and shareholder returns, while asking its existing workforce to absorb repeated cuts.

Xbox Ally and Xbox Series X |S consoles are about to get a big AMD -shaped boost.
Yesterday, AMD and Microsoft revealed that FSR 4.1 is coming to the entire suite of current-gen Xbox devices . That includes Xbox Ally (base model), Xbox Ally X, and Xbox Series X|S consoles.
FSR 4.1 is an upscaling technology that allows games to render images at a lower resolution, passing overhead to performance. Then, FSR 4.1 upscales the image to create a sharper image, granting the appearance of higher native resolution. Technologies like FSR and DLSS have been boosting the lifespan of older and less-powerful hardware for some time now, and given the on-going RAMpocalypse and component crisis, anything that extends the usability of more affordable hardware is a win in my book.
But, when can we expect to get our hands (and eyes) on it? Here's what our sources are telling us so far.
FSR 4.1 will become available to Xbox Series X|S game developers in the next couple of weeks . Some partner developers have already had early access in preview builds, and will enable FSR 4.1 earlier than others. In the AMD video above, the firm used Blood of Dawnwalker to demonstrates FSR 4.1 boosts on Xbox Ally devices, so you can probably expect that to be among the first batch.
For Xbox Ally X and the Xbox Ally base model, AMD and ASUS will ship updated drives to the Armoury Crate's new "Preview Update" segment by Friday, Oct 23. The new preview segment which lets users test out early builds if they don't mind risking some bugs and polish, similar to the Xbox and Windows Insider programs.
Developers that have enabled FSR 4.1 on existing PC games will automatically get enhanced when the drivers go live on Xbox Ally devices.
On Xbox Series X|S console, FSR 4.1 won't be retroactively injected into existing games. Developers will have to implement it into their existing games via updates , or support it out of the box in future games.
Sources tell me that there is a "handful" of FSR 4.1-enhanced titles slated for the holiday season on Xbox Series X|S, with a steady feed of new games gaining FSR 4.1 throughout 2027 and beyond.
FSR 4.1 should provide a meaningful quality bump for all sorts of games across Xbox Series X|S and Xbox Ally X and the base model, but perhaps more so on the lower-end devices. The Xbox Series S has been notorious for performance trade offs, with developers struggling with the irregular RAM allocation.
Games on Xbox Series X|S that presently trade resolution down for frame rates should get noticeably sharper even in performance mode when implemented.
People have been using apps like Optiscaler on Github to inject FSR 4 on devices like the Steam Deck , and the results have been impressive, but setting it up can be a chore. Native, official support should bring a ton of performance benefits for the Xbox range across the board without the headaches of using workarounds.
As soon as it's available, I'll be demonstrating how it all works in practice right here on Windows Central.
The big question is ... will GTA 6 support it? Time will tell.

articles.title_orig: Germany’s Merz says EU does not want a trade war with China but will defend itself
articles.title_zh: Germany’s Merz says EU does not want a trade war with China but will defend itself
articles.content_orig:
European leaders are talking a big game on China, but will avoid a full-blown trade war due to internal division and fear of retaliation: analysts
The European Union is likely to avoid a full-blown trade confrontation with China due to internal divisions in the bloc and fear of retaliation, according to a prominent research firm.
But the bloc would “continue to pull its punches” in any confrontation with Beijing due to a lack of consensus among and within Europe’s member states, the London-based Capital Economics said at an event in Hong Kong on Wednesday.
The EU also had “concerns over retaliation” if it stepped up trade tensions with China, the research firm said, and held “lingering hopes to save the rules-based global trading system” that had helped Europe in the past.

articles.content_orig:
In an exclusive sit-down with Sean Hannity, President Donald Trump announced that President Xi Jinping has committed to purchasing 200 Boeing jets, boosting American manufacturing.
Boeing's largest 737 MAX aircraft has received Federal Aviation Administration certification, clearing the way for deliveries of a jet with 1,555 orders that represent a third of the company's outstanding 737 MAX order book.
The FAA announced Tuesday that it had certified the 737 MAX 10 after years of regulatory and safety reviews, removing a major hurdle for Boeing as it prepares to begin deliveries to airlines in the coming months.
Boeing said the aircraft has received orders from more than 30 customers worldwide, making the MAX 10 a key part of the company's commercial airplane backlog.
The approval also marks a significant milestone for Boeing's 737 MAX program, which has received 7,350 orders across the aircraft family, with nearly 2,500 planes delivered through the end of September 2026.
FAA PROPOSES $350K FINE AGAINST CHARTER COMPANY OVER UNAUTHORIZED FLIGHTS
A Boeing 737 MAX 10 test aircraft stands on the tarmac during an event marking the FAA certification of the aircraft at Boeing's Everett Delivery Center in Everett, Washington, on October 20, 2026. (REUTERS/Jason Redmond / Reuters)
"Completing the certification program clears the path for us to deliver a Boeing airplane that will set a new standard in commercial aviation," Stephanie Pope , president and CEO of Boeing Commercial Airplanes, said in a statement.
"The 737-10 offers greater capacity, longer range and the best seat economics in its class, a platform that will create more value and opportunities for airlines around the world," Pope added.
A logo is seen on the Boeing stand on the opening day of the Farnborough International Airshow 2024, southwest of London on July 22, 2024. (JUSTIN TALLIS/AFP via Getty Images / Getty Images)
The 737 MAX 10, the largest aircraft in Boeing's single-aisle MAX family, can seat up to 230 passengers, although airlines will typically configure the jet for 185 to 210 passengers in a two-class layout, according to Boeing. The aircraft has a range of up to 3,100 nautical miles.
Certification followed an extensive FAA safety review and testing program. Boeing said the process involved nearly 1,000 test flights, more than 2,000 flight hours and 1,000 hours of ground testing.
The aircraft includes safety enhancements, among them an updated flight-control system and an enhanced angle-of-attack sensor. Boeing said those improvements will eventually become standard across the 737 MAX family.
Boeing Co. 737 MAX airplanes at the company's manufacturing facility in Renton, Washington, on Wednesday, April 15, 2026. (M. Scott Brauer/Bloomberg via Getty Images / Getty Images)
"The FAA's decision follows a thorough review of the aircraft's design and safety requirements," FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said. "We will continue to hold Boeing to the highest safety standards as the company begins production of the 737 MAX-10."
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy also welcomed the approval, highlighting its significance for the US aerospace manufacturing industry.
"This is a major win for American manufacturing and our nation's status as a global aviation powerhouse," Duffy said in the FAA's announcement.

The certification means all four variants of Boeing's 737 MAX family have now received FAA approval, following the certification of the smaller 737 MAX 7 earlier this year.

articles.title_orig: Final Fantasy Resonance Nintendo Switch 1 vs. 2 differences detailed
articles.title_zh: Final Fantasy Resonance Nintendo Switch 1 vs. 2 differences detailed
articles.content_orig:
by Jordan Rudek - October 20, 2026, 9:00 am EDT Discuss in talkback!
There’s no need for remakes of classic Final Fantasy. We’re already there.
The whiplash I felt between the initial reveal of Final Fantasy Resonance and eventually playing both the eShop demo and PAX West demo still makes my neck tingle before bedtime. You’ll find fewer fans more nostalgic for classic, turn-based Final Fantasy from the NES and SNES days than I am. I’ve yearned for Square Enix to bring this franchise back to its 8 and 16-bit roots, and I’ve happily made do with Octopath Traveler and Bravely Default, among others. However, my longing for more titles like Final Fantasy 1, 4, and 6, has also been made worse by things like the Pixel Remasters. Little did I know that an experience born from mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius would not just slake this mighty thirst; Final Fantasy Resonance would make a Dragoon-like leap to the top of my game of the year list.
Following the journey of Rain, a knight of the kingdom of Grandshelt, and his friend and confidant Lasswell, Resonance sees the world embroiled in a battle against The Sworn Six, a group of armored warriors who seek to destroy the elemental crystals belonging to each realm. At first, the faceless villains seem to be defined only by their pursuit of revenge and destruction, but as the story plays out, you learn about their individual backgrounds and convictions. These aren’t Kefka-esque knaves who would see the world burn only for pleasure; there’s a depth to them and a connection between them and the party of friends and allies you accrue along the way. As great as it is to see how Rain’s relationship with his companions grows, with Lasswell and Fina in particular, there are numerous side characters, including a Final Fantasy stalwart, whose appearances and story beats are incredibly memorable.
Normally, I might leave the art and visuals of a review closer to the end, especially for an RPG, where the world and story often have a bit more impact on one’s enjoyment of the game. I can do no such thing here. Final Fantasy Resonance is an absolute feast for the senses, and I couldn’t help but grin like an absolute moron as I explored new towns and unlocked new abilities, espers, and visions. One of the great joys here is in the spaces between towns and dungeons, where you get to retrieve ethereal versions of Final Fantasy series heroes like Cloud, Cecil, and Lightning, each of whom can be paired with one of your party members to enhance their spell and skill repertoire, while also growing alongside them to provide a number of buffs and stat bonuses. When you’re able to stun an enemy and call forth one of your visions for a final smash, a CG cutscene plays out briefly before the HD-2D version of that hero flies in for devastating effect. This is on top of the dramatic CG entrances of the espers that can be summoned by Fina and function as a temporary fifth party member. There’s also been a massive leap in terms of the overall HD-2D presentation, with cities feeling much more lifelike and to scale, compared to something recent like Octopath Traveler 0. Standing outside Grandshelt Castle is enough to leave one awestruck, but tarry not too long, and make your way to the next-door Colosseum instead.
The Colosseum isn’t the only Final Fantasy throwback; in fact, Resonance is filled to the brim with series charm and references. The soundtrack waffles between familiar tunes and new ones with just a hint of the classics. The version of “Battle on the Big Bridge” that I first encountered while aboard the airship had me pumping my fist so hard I pulled a muscle. Enemy sprites from Final Fantasy 4 and 6 especially are a welcome HD-2D sight, as are the familiar espers like Ifrit, Shiva, and Titan that join your ranks after you prove yourself a worthy opponent in combat. Which brings me to the biggest departure from classic Final Fantasy: the battle system.
Combining a number of familiar elements and then adding a fun wrinkle on top, Resonance’s combat features turn-based action and a novel reward system for wearing your opponent down. Enemies have a stagger meter below their health bar that leaves them stunned once you deplete it, but if you manage to stun every foe on screen, your entire team of four gets a bonus turn to attack, which is then followed by an ultimate ability from one of your equipped visions. The peak of satisfaction (and damage) is when your party can exploit a boss’ weakness multiple times in the bonus round and then have a hero like Cecil or Squall come in with their light and fire elemental finishers to knock your opponent into next week. Certain enemies, especially later in the game, have stout defenses that protect their precious health, and so you can opt for attacks that prioritize depleting the stagger meter and then switch to other moves once you have an opening.
I have to return to the characters, because there are so many small moments between them that conjure feelings of joy, humor, and empathy. One of my favorite duos is engineer Lid and hopeless flirt Jake. Lid with hammer in hand has no problem bonking the crap out of Jake whenever his lude comments stop giving harmless fun and encroach on perverted creeper territory. There’s almost a Palom and Porom, or Edgar and Relm-type relationship between them, and it’s fun to see non-MMO Final Fantasy characters engaging in antics like these. A fitting foil to these interactions is that of Rain and Lasswell, who push each other to be the best versions of themselves. Underneath that, though, are feelings of inferiority that Lasswell has to come to terms with. Seeing the pair’s ups and downs and eventual reaching of their potential makes for an excellent narrative arc.
The pacing of the story has similar peaks and valleys, tending towards a bit more open at times and a bit heavier at others. Some of the mobile trappings seem to rear their head here, such as the division of the game into chapters or the simplified, single-use dungeon spaces, but the more I played, the less I found these elements to be a distraction. Instead, they helped to keep things moving and respect my time over the course of the 30-hour story. I also really enjoyed being able to spend 5-10 minutes on a side quest or hunting down a new esper while enjoying the pleasant airship traveling music. That said, one of the major twists of the game is a bit confounding, but the developers must have realized that since they have one of your party members stand ready to explain and clarify it after that knowledge comes to light.
What’s harder to put into words is the feeling of playing and experiencing Final Fantasy Resonance. I can say without question that it makes me feel like I’m back in elementary school and taking Cecil through his Paladin’s journey or watching Cyan chase the ghost train as it speeds away with his wife and child. This has always been what Final Fantasy was to me, and the nostalgia has been hitting me in waves the more time I’ve spent with Resonance, a title that has only grown more fitting. What were once complaints about the bombastic displays of light and text in combat have given way to the satisfying challenges of the bosses and the unique gauntlets that have to be overcome to progress the story. The mobile roots of Final Fantasy Resonance are there to notice, but I’m happy to say they have no meaningful impact on one’s enjoyment.
The more I played—the more times I struggled to put down my Switch 2 or Pro Controller—the more convinced I was that this is both the follow-up and the legacy of 2D Final Fantasy. I've pined for years to see this beloved series return to its roots, instead of leaning into genres that don't really represent what Final Fantasy is. Resonance, more than anything else, understands what made early Final Fantasy so endearing and enduring. If you've missed fully turn-based battles, quirky pixelated characters, and all of the classic ‘90s Final Fantasy ch

articles.title_orig: Australian politician who was intentionally hit by car loses both her legs
articles.title_zh: Australian politician who was intentionally hit by car loses both her legs
articles.content_orig:
Helen Haines, the Australian MP who was hit by a car in what authorities say was a deliberate attack, has lost both her legs, her husband has confirmed.
Phil Haines said the "horrendous incident" caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind are in good shape". He added that the "good news in all this is that she's alive".
The alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, faces multiple charges and appeared in court for the first time on Wednesday.
Nugent was arrested moments after he allegedly drove his Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP outside her electorate office in the regional town of Wangaratta, about 240km (150miles) northeast of Melbourne.
Haines' "road to recovery will be long and difficult, but we know she is a fighter," her husband said at a press conference in Melbourne where she is being treated.
"She is a determined person who will do her best, with our support and love, to recover. And that is what we hope for."
He thanked hospital staff and people, both in Australia and internationally, who have shown their concern for Haines, and urged those who want to show their support to donate to the Save the Children fund.
"Please keep sending Helen your love," he added.
Earlier on Wednesday, Nugent appeared at the local court to face three charges: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Police said more charges may be laid, including attempted murder.
Nugent - a local from the nearby town of Tarrawingee and known as an environmental campaigner - remained silent and emotionless during his brief court appearance.
He did not apply for bail and is due back in court in February. Court documents show he was also charged with cultivating and possessing cannabis.
In court, Nugent's lawyer said that his client had "mental health concerns" but did not give any further detail.
The court also heard that Nugent has a rare neurological condition - idiopathic transverse myelitis - caused by inflammation of the spinal cord.
Victoria Police said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police (AFP), remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established.
"His motivation for this - what we allege is a deliberate attack - is very much a centrepiece of the investigation," said Victoria Police Commissioner Mike Bush.
"Our people will continue to explore every element, angle and avenue to work that out. It's something that, when we work towards it, discover it, we will present in court."
Nugent was not on the radar of police and there was no intelligence of any threat to Haines before the incident, police said.
Investigators are also looking into whether drug use or medication played a part in the incident and if there was any personal connection between Nugent and Haines.
Nugent's family earlier put out a statement saying they were long-time friends with Haines, who is the independent MP for the regional seat of Indi in Victoria. They described the apparent attack as "devastating and unfathomable".
The incident occurred on Monday afternoon at around 15.35, local time. Moments after the car hit Haines, bystanders pulled Nugent out of the vehicle and detained him.
Jacob and Jackie Evans were among the first on the scene, and said Haines was grateful to them for coming to her aid as she lay severely injured.
"Thank you, you lovely people," is what Haines said to them, according to the Herald Sun.
"She was thanking us, it was incredible," Jackie told Nine's Today programme.
Jacob used a tourniquet he had in a medical kit in his car to help stem the bleeding from one of Haines's legs.
Haines underwent surgery after the incident and lost one of her legs. As of Wednesday morning she has also lost the other leg, her husband Phil told reporters.
The community in Wangaratta, as well as the wider political community, are in shock over the incident in a country where political violence is rare.
Leaders from across the political spectrum have paid tribute to Haines, who was first elected in 2019 and is well regarded by her peers.
Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had spoken to Haines's husband several times since the incident.
In an interview with the national broadcaster ABC, Albanese said threats to female politicians were marked by a "different form of vilification and aggression" such as threats of rape.
There has also been a recent growing trend of threats against "high office holders", with almost one person a week being charged for such offences, police said.
Monday's incident has sparked debate over the level of security for MPs.
Federal police said that individual protection for every one of the country's 226 federal MPs would require "incredible" levels of staffing.
Instead, police assess the need for close personal protection based on a person's role and the threat environment around them, police said.
Australia's Governor-General Sam Mostyn, who spoke at the same press conference as Haines' husband, said this was "a moment for us to pause, and to choose to be better".
"We should do what I imagine Helen would be doing if she was not the victim of this terrible attack - reaching out to those who are terribly distressed by what has happened," she says.
"Most importantly, that we learn or re-learn to exercise our muscle of decency."

articles.title_zh: United Airlines set to open its biggest airport lounge in $2.6 billion overhaul at Houston hub
articles.content_orig:
United Airlines is set to open its biggest airport lounge this week, which it says is the largest in the Americas, as airlines continue to plow money into the facilities for high-spending customers.
The 54,000-square-foot lounge is opening Thursday at George Bush Intercontinental Airport's Terminal B in Houston, part of an overhaul of the facility that includes 22 gates for mainline aircraft.
The airport, with more than 500 departures a day, is United's main connecting hub for flights to and from Latin America.
The new club can seat 800 people and features an outdoor terrace for plane-spotting as well as two full-service bars and buffets.
The lounge, part of United's $2.6 billion investment at the airport's Terminal B, shows how airlines are putting more money into larger spaces for premium-travel demand to attract the growing ranks of elite frequent flyers, co-branded credit card holders and customers just willing to spend more to fly.
American Airlines earlier this month said it is planning its largest-ever lounge at its Charlotte Douglas International Airport hub in North Carolina. Delta Air Lines has expanded both its popular Delta Sky Clubs and its top-tier Delta One Lounges.
Southwest Airlines is building its first-ever network of airport lounges , which are tied to its credit card partner, Chase . Last week, the carrier unveiled mock-ups of the lounges, which it is calling Icon. And JetBlue Airways opened lounges in New York and Boston in the past year.

articles.title_orig: North Korea tells border troops to take ‘resolute action’ if South threatens their safety
articles.title_zh: North Korea tells border troops to take ‘resolute action’ if South threatens their safety
articles.content_orig:
North Korea has told its border troops to take “prompt ​and resolute action” if South Korean forces threaten their safety, state media ​said on Wednesday, raising the risk of a clash along the ⁠heavily armed frontier.
The report came a day after Seoul pledged to punish “resolutely” any ​further provocation by Pyongyang if North Korea acted on threats to strengthen its military ​posture along the border.
North Korean Army Marshal Pak Jong Chon inspected fortifications on the border with South Korea on Tuesday, accompanied by Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong ​Un, KCNA reported.
Kim Yo Jong said new firepower units had “taken their firing positions” at ​the border, KCNA reported.
Tensions between North and South Korea have risen since Pyongyang began fortifying its ‌border ⁠in April 2024. The two countries are separated by the Demilitarized Zone that was established when the Korean War ended in an armistice in 1953.
Seoul says Pyongyang has sent up to 7,000 workers to the border this year, with about 50 ​crossings of the ​Military Demarcation Line, ⁠which bisects the DMZ, to South Korea’s side of the border.
These North Korean brothers spent 10 years planning their escape. Months after reaching freedom, everything changed
On Wednesday, North Korea rejected Seoul’s allegations, with Pak dismissing ​the claim as an “absurd assertion” designed to shift blame, KCNA reported.
The ​North Korean ⁠army knew where the border lay “better than any others” and was only doing what it should within its own territory, Pak said, urging soldiers to turn the border ⁠into an “impregnable ​fortress.”
South Korea said North Korean mines caused ​a border blast last month that seriously wounded two of its soldiers, and called on Pyongyang to suspend the ​fortification work.

articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.content_orig:
You cannot fully block the two critical PHP flaws called PHP2Shell before today's fix, and the one setting being passed around as a workaround is not enough on its own, the security firm that suggested it now says.
PHP will release the fix at 14:00 UTC on October 21 for two flaws it rates 9.2 out of 10, and has given no workaround of its own. Until you can install it, what lowers your risk is taking exposed PHP off the internet or behind access controls, cutting what a compromised server can reach, and having the update ready to apply the moment it lands.
Cloudflare says it is seeing early attempts to exploit the flaws, and has pushed emergency rules for sites behind it that it calls a stopgap until you patch. No compromise has been confirmed, the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work, and neither flaw is in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws. PHP has not said which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, or whether any setting changes the risk; it says the full details and the fixed versions come with the release.
At the time of writing, that release was not yet out. So nobody outside the group that found the flaws can test whether a given defense works, which is why the advice below is about lowering risk, not promising safety.
The workaround spreading on social media and security blogs is one line in a PHP configuration file: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 . It turns off Session Upload Progress, a PHP feature that's enabled by default, which records how far a file upload has progressed so another request can check on it.
GMO Flatt Security, a Tokyo security firm, suggested setting it early on October 21, saying it could not be sure the change fully addresses the flaws but thought it would help with some probability.
Later the same day, the firm walked that back. In an update timestamped 14:00 Japan time (05:00 UTC), it said the setting alone is not a complete fix and that attacks getting around it are expected. It told administrators to prepare their update, watch for attack traffic before the release, and apply the fix as soon as it is out.
Two people from the PHP project said the same thing more bluntly. Replying to someone who suggested the upload-progress setting might patch the flaw, Gina Peter Banyard, a PHP core developer and documentation writer funded by the PHP Foundation, wrote : "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP. I sadly know too much." Joe Ferguson, the release manager for the coming PHP 8.6, put it shorter : "ini settings won't save you."
The setting cannot be relied on for two reasons. GMO Flatt expects a way around it but has not said what that is. And the whole idea that the flaw lives in Session Upload Progress is a guess: PHP has not confirmed it, the firm itself said it holds only so far as its own research matches PHP2Shell, and an independent code audit argues the specific bug others describe in that feature does not exist in released PHP. That audit is from an anonymous account and PHP's own code will settle it, but it is one more reason not to treat the setting as a shield.
Not everyone agrees. One vendor, Upwind, still lists the setting as an immediate mitigation , passing along another researcher's analysis rather than its own tests. watchTowr, which reproduced one of the flaws, says there is "no confirmed patch or workaround at this time."
No one is telling you to undo the change. The instruction is only not to count it as protection. PHP's own manual already advises turning the feature off where an application does not use upload progress bars, because the stored file names and field names "are not validated and may contain PHP code." If you turned it on by mistake somewhere that needs it, the only cost is that upload progress bars stop working.
Check that the change is actually in effect on the process that serves web traffic, not on the command line. The setting is INI_PERDIR, so it can be set in php.ini, .htaccess, or .user.ini.
A .user.ini file is read only by the CGI and FastCGI versions of PHP, not by the Apache module, and PHP re-reads it only every 300 seconds by default, so a change there can take five minutes to apply.
Under the Apache module, use .htaccess or the server config. Confirm the value on PHP-FPM or mod_php, whichever serves your site, not on php -i at the shell.
Get ready now. GMO Flatt's advice is to confirm your update steps and the checks you run afterward, rehearse any config change, and line up the people and approvals for a possible emergency restart. When the fix lands, update the runtime that serves web requests, which is PHP-FPM, mod_php, or CGI, not the application on top of it.
PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, 8.2 through 8.5. Which exact versions carry the fix and how far back the flaws extend will be announced with the release.
The Hacker News reported the branch support and the wider background in its earlier coverage of the disclosure.
Where an immediate update is not possible, CERT-EU advises organizations to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied." Banyard put the same point from inside the project: turning a server off for a day "might be the most sensible thing to do. But that is far from a reasonable thing to demand for most people." Short of shutting down, restrict reach: put the site behind a VPN, allowlisted clients, or authenticated access at the edge, and check that traffic cannot reach the origin directly around those controls.
Shrink what an attacker gets if the server is taken over. GMO Flatt's other steps are to reduce the data stored on the server, reduce its privileges, remove stored credentials, including cloud roles, and ensure logging is enabled and kept in a secure location so you can investigate later.
Branches older than 8.2, including 8.1, 7.x, and 5.x, are end-of-life and receive no PHP fixes. For those, upgrade, take the system offline, or isolate it; a Linux distribution or hosting provider may backport a fix on its own schedule.
A web application firewall is a stopgap here, not a fix, and Cloudflare says so itself. It has pushed emergency rules for the known exploit paths, free tier included, which its CTO calls "a STOPGAP only" ahead of patching. Such rules only see traffic that passes through Cloudflare, and they can miss new attack paths as they appear.
Updating WordPress, Laravel, or another application does not update the PHP runtime underneath it; that comes from your server package, host, or container image. On managed or shared hosting, ask your provider when a fixed PHP build will land and have them stand by.
Hosting providers build their packages only after PHP ships the fix: CloudLinux, for one, says its updated packages depend on the upstream release and will be posted when ready.
Exploitation is early and unconfirmed. Cloudflare reports emerging attempts; watchTowr says it reproduced one flaw but has not reported attacks; the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work; and neither flaw was in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws when it was last checked on October 21.
A researcher has posted a video said to demonstrate the exploit chain, and the audit above states that the circulating proof-of-concept code does not fire against released PHP. Treat all of this as a snapshot that can change by the hour.
When the fix ships, check the fixed version for your branch, which versions PHP lists as affected, whether PHP confirms or rejects any setting as a mitigation, and whether the session code changed, which also answers the dispute over where the flaw lives.
The fixed versions and the advisory will appear on php.net and through PHP's GitHub security advisories , where the project assigns its own identifiers. After updating, review your logs for anything that happened before you patched.

articles.title_orig: 'Far-left activist' arrested in France after city hall set on fire amid ongoing protests
articles.title_zh: 'Far-left activist' arrested in France after city hall set on fire amid ongoing protests
articles.content_orig:
Coverage for this event has ended.
President Donald Trump points as he speaks at a midterm campaign rally at Pitt-Greenville Airport in Greenville, N.C., on Tuesday. ( (Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Images)
President Donald Trump on Tuesday vowed to treat potential rioters in the U.S. “very rough,” pointing to the unrest that has gripped France in recent days.
Trump made the remarks during a speech in Greenville, North Carolina, ahead of the midterm elections, after a heckler interrupted him as he campaigned for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley.
“They're crazy, these people. Look at that guy. He's a nutjob,” Trump said, referring to the protester in the crowd.
Trump warned that he would crack down on potential threats, saying he would not allow similar unrest to take hold in the U.S.
“That's what you witness over the last three or four days. You watch nutjobs like him in France ruining their country,” Trump said. “We're not going to put up with it by the way.”
“If a possible threat, which could happen, I hope you won't get angry if I treat them very, very rough, because that's what's going to happen. They're not going to destroy our country.”
Click here to follow the latest updates with the protests in France.
Albanian police have clashed with anti-government protesters for an eighth consecutive day in the capital, Tirana , as demonstrators call for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, according to the Associated Press.
Similar to unrest sweeping across Europe, Albania’s protests have been fueled by discontent over rising fuel costs, the education system and a housing crisis, the AP said.
During the protests, demonstrators reportedly have hurled rocks, flares and firebombs at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.
Rama condemned the protests Tuesday, saying attempts to force political change through violence would never be allowed, according to the AP.
“A wave of stones, an attempt to overthrow the government and change those in power through the imposition of violence — something that will never be allowed to happen, in any form or for any reason,” Rama said Tuesday after a meeting with teachers and representatives of Tirana’s schools.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, attends the fifth session of the UN Permanent Forum on People of African Descent. Türk condemned violence and vandalism during protests across Europe while urging police to avoid excessive force. (Getty Images)
UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk on Tuesday condemned riots that have erupted across Europe over rising living costs, urging police to respond lawfully and calling for accountability for protesters who commit acts of violence and vandalism.
“I deplore the actions of those exploiting protests to commit acts of violence and vandalism against public and private property. They should be held individually accountable,” Turk said.
“I am concerned by reports of unnecessary and excessive use of force against protesters, including children. States must ensure that any law enforcement response remains lawful, necessary and proportionate. Allegations of unlawful use of force must be investigated promptly, effectively and independently, with accountability and effective remedies for victims.”
Türk called for “inclusive and safe dialogue” between governments and protesters to prioritize human rights concerns .
“I further urge States to engage protesters, particularly young people, in meaningful, inclusive and constructive dialogue, and to take concrete steps to address legitimate and fundamental human rights concerns over education, public services, housing, the rising cost of living and inequality,” he said.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni speaks during a joint statement in Rome on Jan. 23, 2026. (Remo Casilli/Reuters)
Italy on Tuesday announced a series of tougher security measures following reports of looting and vandalism that rocked Milan and other cities over the weekend.
The measures include deploying 500 additional military personnel in Milan, requiring offenders or their parents to pay for damaged property, and imposing harsher penalties on protesters who engage in violence.
The additional military personnel will work alongside law enforcement through the end of year, while the government plans to expand judicial resources to ensure legal consequences for offenders, including some teenagers.
Under the measures, minors or their parents would also be required to pay for property they damage, the council said.
“Of course, they can oppose it, but in the meantime, the parents of that boy who enjoyed smashing everything will have to pay. And whoever suffered the damage will be able to recover everything, from that family's assets, even from any money the state may owe them,” the council said in a release statement.
The council added that nearly 200 officers have been injured and property damage in Milan alone is estimated at around 1 million euros, citing Confcommercio, Italy’s largest business association.
Protesters set fire to the town hall in Limoges Haute-Vienne in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region of France on Oct. 17, 2026. (Elise Cabane / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images)
The U.S. Embassy in France is warning Americans to steer clear of violent protests as unrest sparked curfews and raised concerns about travel disruptions across the country.
The riots — fueled by a range of grievances, including rising living costs and mass migration — have been reported across France, with protests reported in cities including Paris, Lille and Lyon.
Authorities have imposed localized curfews as a result.
The embassy said in a Monday statement that partial curfews had been introduced in several French cities, with additional restrictions possible.
"Following the October 17 protests that turned violent, media report the Prime Minister’s office introduced partial curfews for Monday, October 19 and Tuesday, October 20 in several cities across France, including Lille," the embassy said.
"Media report more curfews may follow for parts of Paris and in prefectures across the country, and that scattered protests could continue."
This is an excerpt of an article by Fox News Digital's Andrea Margolis.
France's Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu leaves the Interior Ministry in Paris on October 19, 2026. (JULIEN DE ROSA / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Tuesday accused far-left groups of organizing “insurrectionary” plans linked to the riots that erupted over the weekend.
During a raucous parliamentary session, Lecornu blasted “the planning, in certain locations, of an insurrectionary plan led by far-left and ultra-left fringe groups,” according to the French National Assembly.
Lecornu said the riots were joined by criminals seeking to “loot and destroy” property, according to the French National Assembly.
"No one will impose their political agenda through violence,” he added.
"Peaceful demonstrations have their rightful place in our Republic. Arson, looting, and attacks have none," he said.
The violent protests over the cost of living in Paris have prompted French authorities to deploy military forces to reinforce police ahead of Saturday’s planned demonstrations , Reuters reported.
Trash burns during clashes between protestors and police officers during a demonstration against rising living costs, joining students' grievances, in Paris, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Emma Da Silva)
President Donald Trump on Tuesday dismissed concerns that a socialist agenda could spark unrest in the U.S. similar to riots in France, arguing that the two countries are fundamentally different.

articles.title_orig: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.title_zh: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.content_orig:
United States Special Envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian leaders on the Ukraine war following “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway.
Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday in the city in northwestern Russia, as the US pushes for an end to the war that began more than four and a half years ago with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Zelenskyy in recent weeks and has suggested that someone else should negotiate on Kyiv’s behalf. The remarks signalled a new low in their relationship, while Zelenskyy has accused the US of suspending crucial intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the talks between Witkoff and Zelenskyy as “positive”, adding that the US envoy would share the results with Putin. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also attended the talks with Zelenskyy, but did so virtually because of illness. Kushner is also expected to attend the meeting with Putin remotely.
“He’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side – and let’s see if we can make some progress,” Rubio said.
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland also attended the talks in Oslo. Representatives from the European Union and NATO were present. Following Tuesday’s talks, Zelenskyy said “very, very important” intelligence from the US had been restored.
Zelenskyy has also accused Washington of slowing down the internet service, Starshield, which is crucial for Ukraine’s battlefield operations. Starshield is the military-grade equivalent of Starlink and is also developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Rubio dismissed Zelenskyy’s accusations, saying Trump had “nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield”. Musk disputes this and says such decisions can only be made by the US military and president.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk ordered the slowdown of the service, citing US officials and people familiar ⁠with the matter.
As diplomatic efforts intensify, Russia and Ukraine continue to trade long-range attacks.
At least one person was killed and two were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack in Russia’s western Bryansk ⁠region on Wednesday, Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said on Telegram.
The Ukrainian Emergency Service said two people were killed in a Russian attack on a high-rise building in the Sviatoshinsky district of the capital, Kyiv.

articles.title_orig: Russian prime minister says Russia-China trade turnover grows more than 30-fold over 25 years
articles.title_zh: Russian prime minister says Russia-China trade turnover grows more than 30-fold over 25 years
articles.content_orig:
Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said on Wednesday that trade turnover between Russia and China has increased more than 30-fold over the past 25 years despite external pressure.
Speaking at a meeting in St. Petersburg with Chinese Premier Li Qiang ahead of the 31st regular meeting between the two countries' heads of government, Mishustin added that bilateral trade was growing steadily, with nearly all transactions conducted in national currencies, the ruble and the yuan.
"Despite increased external pressure, Russia-China trade and economic cooperation has demonstrated strong momentum: over the past 25 years, our bilateral trade turnover has increased more than 30-fold," he said.
More than 90 projects across various sectors, from metallurgy to agriculture, are currently in the portfolio of the relevant bilateral commission, Mishustin said.
"Today, the share of national currencies in bilateral trade is already close to 100%," the Russian prime minister said, adding that bilateral investment was also increasing.
Mishustin called China a key economic partner, pledged continued reliable energy supplies, cited peaceful nuclear projects as a promising area, and noted that Russia remains China's top oil supplier with Power of Siberia -- the gas conduit stretching from Siberia to China -- running steadily.
"Russia will continue to reliably ensure uninterrupted energy supplies. We are also ready to strengthen cooperation in the energy sector," he said.
Bilateral agricultural trade grew by more than one-third in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, Mishustin said.
Russian products marketed under the Made in Russia brand had demonstrated their quality and were gaining popularity in China, he added.
The two countries should expand the range of goods traded between them to meet consumer demand, the Russian prime minister said.
Mutual tourist flows between Russia and China increased by approximately 50% in the first half of 2026, Mishustin said. He also called for more active modernization of border crossing points and an expansion of the geographical reach of air transport links between the countries.
Li Qiang said Russian-Chinese relations entered a new stage of more substantive and accelerated development under the strategic leadership of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
He described the regular meeting as an important opportunity to comprehensively review bilateral cooperation, address existing issues and translate agreements reached by the leaders into practical action and tangible results for their peoples.
Li said that despite changes in the international situation over recent decades, the two countries' commitment to good-neighborly relations, friendship, cooperation and development had remained unchanged.
"Adhering to the principles of non-alignment, non-confrontation and not targeting third parties, we have upheld mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation," he said, adding that Russia and China had established a model of high-level mutual trust and cooperation between major powers and neighboring countries.
The regular meeting between the Russian and Chinese heads of government is being held for the 31st time. The previous meeting took place in China in early November 2025, in Hangzhou and Beijing.

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after investors rotated into defensive assets and priced in rising expectations that midterm election outcomes could reverse recent federal spending cuts.
Capital has increasingly shifted toward defensive sectors, which are widely recognized for delivering resilient earnings and dependable cash flows during times of macroeconomic uncertainty as reported by Axios. Beyond this safe-haven rotation, market sentiment was bolstered by growing expectations that Democrats could gain ground in upcoming midterm elections.
A political shift could lead to the rollback or easing of federal healthcare spending cuts implemented under President Trump's 2025 spending bill.A potential reversal of those reductions is viewed positively by investors, as it would protect vital funding streams and preserve demand for pharmaceuticals, clinical care, and related healthcare services. With regulatory headwinds potentially diminishing and macroeconomic caution lingering, healthcare equities saw broad-based buying across the industry.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Azenta's shares are extremely volatile and have had 33 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock dropped 7.9% on the news that capital-intensive growth equities experienced sharp sell-offs as elevated bond yields restricted market appetite for risk. As reported by CNBC, rising Treasury yields put direct, outsized pressure on long-duration assets, because higher interest rates increase the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, thereby diminishing the present value of the distant cash flows that early-stage drug and life sciences companies rely on to justify their high valuations.
Furthermore, CNBC analysts noted that investors are increasingly reassessing the impact of these elevated interest rates on overall economic growth and corporate debt-servicing capacity, which is particularly concerning for clinical-stage healthcare firms that must continuously tap debt markets to fund research and development.
Ultimately, CNBC observed that a broader flight to safety temporarily outweighed inflation fears across the market, prompting capital to aggressively exit these riskier, high-multiple healthcare assets and flow toward the relative stability of the Treasury market and blue-chip equities.
Azenta is up 5.7% since the beginning of the year, but at $35.30 per share, it is still trading 17.4% below its 52-week high of $42.73 from October 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Azenta's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $335.62.

articles.title_orig: Opinion | Can China turn national power into world leadership?
articles.title_zh: Opinion | Can China turn national power into world leadership?
articles.content_orig:
China has all the signs of world-topping national strength but whether other countries accept its leadership will depend on what’s on offer
As turbulence grows in many countries, it is tempting to ask if there is a global hegemon that can sort everything out fairly.
Our latest projections of national strength for 2027 take into account resources, territory, economic strength and military power. They still put China in first place, with its lead over other countries widening. But when might China move beyond leading the ranking to exert decisive influence over the world’s trouble spots and become a global arbiter?
To explore that question, we should first look at how states have assessed national power. Ancient rulers counted people, revenues, troops, ships and resources but these were separate assessments, not a single measure of national power.

articles.title_orig: Witkoff to present Putin with peace proposal after talks with Zelensky
articles.title_zh: Witkoff to present Putin with peace proposal after talks with Zelensky
articles.content_orig:
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff is holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin about ending the war in Ukraine, a day after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy insisted that any negotiations over his country's future must include Kyiv.
Speaking alongside the leaders of Finland and Norway in Oslo late on Tuesday, Zelenskyy said discussions with U.S. officials had been constructive and that Washington had reaffirmed its commitment to providing Ukraine with security guarantees.
But he stressed that any agreement concerning Ukraine's future would be acceptable only if Kyiv had a seat at the negotiating table.
"It can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations," he said, adding that he had discussed the reported proposal of a trilateral meeting between the U.S., China, and Russia to negotiate an end to the almost five-year conflict with U.S. representatives. "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine," he said.
At the start of talks in St. Petersburg, Russia announced it would release an American man who had been "wrongfully detained," according to the State Department, on charges that he was a Ukrainian mercenary. Witkoff thanked Putin for the release of retired teacher Stephen Hubbard, according to Russian media .
On Tuesday, Zelenskyy said the Oslo meeting had included discussions on NATO's Article 5 – which says that an armed attack against one member constitutes an attack on all – and "different kinds of security guarantees," which Witkoff will share with the Russians. "We will hear his feedback in one day," Zelenskyy said Tuesday.
The developments come amid heightened tensions between the U.S. and Ukraine as President Donald Trump and Zelenskyy have traded public criticism. Trump has accused the Ukrainian president of not wanting peace, while Zelenskyy has argued that Washington's easing of sanctions on Russia, including a deal on diesel , risks prolonging the conflict.
Overnight, Russia struck energy and civilian targets across Ukraine, resulting in at least one casualty, according to local media reports. It follows Trump's Oct. 11 claim that he had brokered an "energy ceasefire," whereby the countries would refrain from striking each other's energy infrastructure amid high diesel prices.
Ukraine paused such attacks for three days before resuming them, citing continuing Russian attacks.
On Tuesday, Zelenskyy confirmed that U.S. intelligence had resumed sharing early warnings of Russian attacks, while discussions continued over SpaceX's Starlink connectivity and Patriot air defense systems.
